mainTopic: Unseparated מעשר עני and the amount of טבל for lashes; the new משנה on eating holy foods wrongly, and רבי שמעון's derivations from the פסוק
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about מעשר עני of דמאי. רבי אליעזר says you only name the portion and do not need to separate it. רב יוסף suggests the dispute is about whether unseparated מעשר עני makes produce טבל. אביי rejects this, so the גמרא explains that everyone agrees it makes טבל, and the argument is only about whether עמי הארץ can be trusted to separate it. Next, two versions of ריש לקיש disagree on whether רבי שמעון's 'any amount' of טבל for lashes applies to flour too. A ברייתא supports רבי ירמיה's version, that it does. A new משנה then lists more cases that bring forty lashes, such as eating ביכורים before the reading and eating holy food outside its place. It also teaches that a לאו which comes with a 'get up and do' command does not bring lashes. The גמרא says the ביכורים ruling follows רבי עקיבא, who holds like רבי שמעון. It then brings רבי שמעון's ברייתא, which uses one קל וחומר after another to find a new lashes-rule in each word of the פסוק. The last word, נדריך for the עולה, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: name the portion, no need to separate it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי אליעזר's view on מעשר עני of דמאי: one designates it by name but does not need to physically separate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He calls the name on it, but he does not need to separate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from just before this section. It gives רבי אליעזר's position: with מעשר עני of דמאי, you just name a portion, and you do not have to set it aside and hand it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים in this ברייתא require actually separating מעשר עני from דמאי. רבי אליעזר asks for less: only a verbal designation. The next steps try to figure out what this difference is really about.

keyTerms.meaning: Calls the name: verbally designates a portion as a tithe
To separate: physically set the portion aside
Poor man's tithe, given to the poor in certain years
Produce bought from an עם הארץ, where we are not sure whether it was tithed

phrases.english: He calls the name,
phrases.notes: He says out loud that a certain portion is מעשר עני, without actually moving it aside.

phrases.english: but he does not need to separate it.

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹרֵא אֶת הַשֵּׁם, וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַפְרִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous section of the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, for מעשר עני of דמאי one only designates it by name and does not need to separate it.

steps.title: Suggestion: the dispute is whether unseparated מעשר עני makes produce into טבל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף suggests that חכמים hold unseparated מעשר עני makes produce into טבל, and רבי אליעזר holds it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that they argue about this: one Sage holds that when מעשר עני was certainly not taken, the produce is טבל, and the other Sage holds that it is not טבל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the ברייתא as proof. It suggests the two sides really argue about whether missing מעשר עני turns food into forbidden טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If unseparated מעשר עני makes food טבל, then even doubtful דמאי needs separation, which is the view of חכמים. If it does not make טבל, there is less reason to bother, which would explain רבי אליעזר's lighter rule. This would mean the question of טבל depends on a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (a way of proposing an explanation)
They disagree
Certain: here, a case where the tithe was definitely not taken
Makes it into טבל (produce forbidden until tithed)

phrases.english: What, is it not that they disagree about this:
that one Sage holds: when it is certain, it makes it tevel,
phrases.notes: Meaning: when מעשר עני was definitely not taken, the produce counts as טבל.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: even when certain, it does not make it tevel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא as the source of a deeper dispute
steps.raayaObject: Whether unseparated מעשר עני makes produce into טבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's dispute between חכמים and רבי אליעזר about מעשר עני of דמאי

steps.title: אביי: then they should have argued about the certain case
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects: if the real argument were about the certain case, the תנאים should have argued about the certain case directly, not about the doubtful case of דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, instead of arguing about the doubtful case, let them argue about the certain case!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the suggestion. If the argument is really about produce where the tithe was definitely not taken, why would the ברייתא frame it around doubtful דמאי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dispute is usually taught in the case that shows the point most clearly. Arguing about a doubtful case when the real issue is the certain case would be strange. So the suggestion from step 2 does not fit the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces an objection)
Instead of disagreeing about...
Its doubtful case
Let them disagree

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: If so,
instead of disagreeing about its doubtful case,
phrases.notes: The doubtful case is דמאי, where we are not sure the tithe was taken.

phrases.english: let them disagree about the certain case!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי הָכִי, אַדְּמִיפַּלְגִי בִּסְפֵיקוֹ, לִיפַּלְגוּ בְּוַדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proposed reading of the dispute
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's suggestion that the ברייתא's dispute is about whether certain unseparated מעשר עני makes טבל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the issue were the certain case, the תנאים would have argued about the certain case, not the doubtful one.

steps.title: New explanation: everyone agrees it makes טבל; they argue about trusting עמי הארץ
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree that certain unseparated מעשר עני makes טבל. They argue about whether עמי הארץ can be trusted to have separated מעשר עני: one side says yes because it is only money, and חכמים say no because it is a bother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that the certain case makes it טבל. Here they argue about this: one Sage holds that עמי הארץ were not suspected about מעשר עני of דמאי, since it is just money and they do separate it. חכמים hold that since the matter is a bother to him, he does not separate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier suggestion and gives a new reason for the dispute. The question is now about the behavior of עמי הארץ, not about the law of טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר עני has no holiness; it is only money owed to the poor. One side thinks an עם הארץ would still set it aside, so with דמאי we can just name it. חכמים think the effort involved means he probably skipped it, so we must separate it ourselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Unlearned people, not careful about tithing
Were suspected
Money, a monetary matter with no holiness
Effort, a bother

steps.whatToRemember: The final explanation: everyone agrees that unseparated מעשר עני makes produce טבל. The ברייתא's dispute is only about whether עמי הארץ can be trusted to separate it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the ברייתא as proof against the view that unseparated מעשר עני makes produce טבל, so that view still stands for the discussion of מלקות.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees that the certain case makes it tevel.
And here they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: לֹא נֶחְשְׁדוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: One Sage holds: amei ha'aretz were not suspected
about poor man's tithe of demai.
Since it is only money, he does separate it.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: כֵּיוָן דִּטְרִיחָא לֵיהּ מִילְּתָא
phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold: since the matter is a bother to him,
he does not separate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection by moving the dispute to a different issue
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the basis of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's dispute is about whether certain unseparated מעשר עני makes produce טבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees it makes טבל. The dispute is whether עמי הארץ are trusted to separate מעשר עני.

steps.title: רב ביבי: the dispute is only about a wheat kernel, not flour
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's argument over how much טבל one must eat to get lashes, רב ביבי quotes ריש לקיש: the argument is about a single kernel of wheat, but for flour everyone requires a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much must one eat from טבל, etc. רב ביבי said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: the dispute is about wheat, but with flour everyone agrees it is a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה. רבי שמעון says any amount of טבל brings lashes, and חכמים say a כזית. ריש לקיש limits where that argument applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this version, רבי שמעון's 'any amount' applies only to eating one whole kernel of wheat. For flour, even רבי שמעון agrees you need a כזית. The text does not say why, but a whole kernel seems to count as a complete item in a way that loose flour does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce that has not yet been tithed and is forbidden to eat
A dispute
A kernel of wheat
Flour
An olive-bulk, the standard minimum amount for eating

steps.confusionAlert: Even this version agrees that רבי שמעון holds 'any amount.' It only limits that rule to a whole kernel of wheat. For flour, everyone requires a כזית.

phrases.english: How much must one eat from untithed produce, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
The dispute is about a kernel of wheat,
but with flour, everyone agrees it is an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion on another line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between רבי שמעון and חכמים applies only to a kernel of wheat. For flour, everyone requires a כזית.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the dispute applies to flour too
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes ריש לקיש differently: the argument applies to flour just as it applies to a wheat kernel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: just as there is a dispute in this case, so there is a dispute in that case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, competing version of what ריש לקיש said. In this version, the argument covers flour too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ירמיה's version, רבי שמעון holds that even a tiny bit of flour from טבל brings lashes. So the two versions disagree on whether רבי שמעון's 'any amount' rule is limited to a whole kernel.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there is a dispute in this case
So there is a dispute in that case

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of ריש לקיש. רב ביבי says the dispute is only about a wheat kernel. רבי ירמיה says the dispute also applies to flour.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Just as there is a dispute in this case,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the wheat kernel, and 'that' in the next line is the flour.

phrases.english: so there is a dispute in that case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of ריש לקיש's statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between רבי שמעון and חכמים applies to flour just as it applies to a wheat kernel.

steps.title: The Ant and the Wheat Kernel Seem to Exclude Flour
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's back-and-forth between רבי שמעון and the חכמים, the גמרא infers that רבי שמעון only gives lashes for a whole wheat kernel, not for a tiny bit of flour. This challenges רבי ירמיה's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבי שמעון said to the חכמים, 'Don't you agree that someone who eats an ant of any size is liable?' They answered, 'That is because it is a whole creature, as it was created.' He said, 'One wheat kernel is also whole, as it was created.' So a kernel, yes; flour, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and reads it closely. It shows that רבי שמעון's argument is built on the wheat kernel being whole, so it seems he would not give lashes for a tiny amount of flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה said ריש לקיש holds that the argument applies to flour too. But רבי שמעון's own reasoning ('it is whole, like when it was created') only works for a whole kernel. That fits רב ביבי's version: for flour, everyone needs a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: An ant
Any amount at all, even the tiniest
In its whole, created form
Flour

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Shimon said to them:
Do you not agree with me
about one who eats an ant of any size
that he is liable?
They said to him: Because it is whole, the way it was created.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: אַף חִטָּה אַחַת כִּבְרִיָּיתָהּ.
phrases.english: He said to them: One wheat kernel is also whole, the way it was created.
A wheat kernel, yes; flour, no!
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own inference. רבי שמעון only argued about a whole kernel, which seems to match רב ביבי's version, not רבי ירמיה's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ירמיה's version of ריש לקיש from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's claim that רבי שמעון gives lashes for any amount of flour too
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's argument depends on the kernel being whole, so it implies no lashes for a tiny amount of flour

steps.title: רבי שמעון Was Arguing on the חכמים' Own Terms
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון himself holds that even any amount of flour brings lashes. He only argued from the whole kernel to win something according to the חכמים' own reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He spoke to them according to their view: 'In my opinion, even flour brings lashes. But according to your opinion, at least agree with me that one wheat kernel is whole, the way it was created.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says רבי שמעון's kernel argument was not his own full position; it was a 'by your own logic' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים gave lashes for a tiny ant because it is whole. רבי שמעון used their reason to say a whole kernel should count too. That does not limit his own view, which covers flour as well. So רבי ירמיה's version still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: According to their own words or view
In my own opinion
At least

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי שמעון backed down. His real view is that even a tiny bit of flour brings lashes. The kernel argument was only a 'by your own logic' point.

phrases.english: He was speaking to them according to their view:
In my view, even flour too brings lashes;
but according to you,
at least agree with me
that one wheat kernel is whole, the way it was created.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the speaker's intent: the argument was made on the other side's own terms
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון only gives lashes for a whole kernel, not for flour
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון gives lashes even for any amount of flour; the kernel point was only aimed at the חכמים' logic

steps.title: Why the חכמים Reject the Kernel Comparison
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that a living creature is significant even when tiny, but a wheat kernel is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: a creature with a soul is significant; a wheat kernel is not significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the חכמים say back to רבי שמעון's kernel argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'whole' is not enough by itself. For the חכמים, what makes a tiny ant count is that it is a living creature, which is important. A kernel of wheat does not have that importance, so it still needs a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature with a soul, a living being
Significant, important

phrases.english: And the Rabbis respond:
a creature with a soul is significant;
a wheat kernel is not significant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the חכמים' side of the debate after step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים do not accept רבי שמעון's kernel argument
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only a living creature is important enough to count at any size; a kernel is not

steps.title: A ברייתא Supports רבי ירמיה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון saying that any amount brings lashes, and that the כזית measure applies only to bringing a קרבן. This supports רבי ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבי ירמיה: רבי שמעון says any amount is enough for lashes. The כזית measure was only said for bringing a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי ירמיה's version of ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says 'any amount' with no limit to whole kernels, so flour is included. He limits the כזית measure to a חטאת brought for eating by mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with his opinion
Lashes
The size of an olive, the usual minimum for eating
An offering, here a חטאת for eating by mistake

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ירמיה, and the ברייתא backs him up, רבי שמעון gives lashes for any amount of טבל, even flour. כזית matters only for bringing a קרבן.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with Rabbi Yirmeya:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא לְמַכּוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Any amount is enough for lashes;
they only said an olive-size
for bringing an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for the view defended in step 8
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's version: the argument applies to flour too
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון says any amount brings lashes and כזית is only for a קרבן

steps.title: New משנה: Eating Holy Food Wrongly and Breaking a פסח Bone
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists cases that bring forty lashes. These are eating ביכורים before the declaration, eating holy food outside its allowed area, and breaking a bone of a pure פסח offering. Leaving over a pure פסח and breaking a bone of an impure one do not bring lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who eats ביכורים before the declaration was said over them, קדשי קדשים outside the curtains, or קדשים קלים and מעשר שני outside the wall, and one who breaks a bone of a pure פסח offering, gets forty lashes. But one who leaves over a pure פסח, or breaks a bone of an impure one, does not get forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists more prohibitions that bring forty lashes, plus two that do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each holy food has a set place or condition for eating it. Eating it before that condition is met, or outside its area, brings lashes. Breaking a bone of a pure פסח brings lashes, but leaving meat over or breaking a bone of an impure פסח does not; the משנה gives no reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
The holiest offerings, eaten only inside the courtyard
The curtains surrounding the משכן courtyard
Offerings of lesser holiness, eaten inside ירושלים
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים
One who leaves meat over past its time

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who eats first fruits
before he recited over them,
phrases.notes: This is the declaration said over ביכורים, from דברים 26:3–10.

phrases.english: most-holy offerings outside the curtains,
offerings of lesser holiness and second tithe
outside the wall of Jerusalem.
One who breaks the bone
of a pure Pesach offering:
he receives forty lashes.
But one who leaves over meat of a pure one
and one who breaks a bone of an impure one
does not receive forty lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוֹכֵל בִּכּוּרִים עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרָא עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה continuing the list of those who receive lashes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating holy food before its condition is met or outside its place, and breaking a bone of a pure פסח, bring forty lashes; leaving over a pure פסח or breaking a bone of an impure one does not

steps.title: Taking the Mother Bird and the Rule of a Prohibition Fixed by Action
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says one who takes the mother bird with her young gets lashes and does not send her away. The חכמים say he sends her and gets no lashes. They give a rule: a לאו that can be fixed by a positive action does not bring lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who takes the mother bird with her young: רבי יהודה says he gets lashes and does not send her away; the חכמים say he sends her away and does not get lashes. This is the rule: any לא תעשה that comes with a 'get up and do' command does not bring lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a dispute about שילוח הקן. It ends with a general rule explaining the חכמים' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids taking the mother and also commands sending her away. For the חכמים, the 'send her' command lets him fix the sin, so there are no lashes as long as he sends her. רבי יהודה holds he is lashed, and then the sending is no longer required.

keyTerms.meaning: The mother bird together with her young
Sends away (the mother bird)
This is the general rule

keyTerms.term: לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ קוּם עֲשֵׂה
keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that comes with a command to take action, which fixes it

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, a לאו that has its own 'get up and do' fix does not bring lashes; you do the fix instead.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule about a לאו שיש בו קום עשה applies across many מצוות, not just the mother bird.

phrases.english: One who takes the mother bird with her young:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לוֹקֶה וְאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּחַ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He is lashed and does not send her away.
And the Rabbis say: He sends her away and is not lashed.
This is the rule:
any negative commandment
that has in it a 'get up and do' command,
one is not liable to lashes for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new case and a general rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: a לאו that comes with a command to take action does not bring lashes; רבי יהודה: one who takes the mother bird is lashed and does not send her

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה's ruling about eating ביכורים before the reading is רבי עקיבא's view. The חכמים say only placing them by the מזבח is essential, not the reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this is the view of רבי עקיבא, taught without his name. But the חכמים say: for ביכורים, placing them is essential, but reading is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by telling us whose opinion the משנה follows on eating ביכורים before the reading. It also shows that the חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 11) said a כהן who eats ביכורים before the reading gets lashes. That only works if the reading is essential. The חכמים hold that only the הנחה is essential, so for them there would be no lashes once the fruit was placed.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught without a name; an unattributed ruling
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
Placing the ביכורים beside the מזבח
Reciting the ביכורים פסוקים
Holds back; is essential, so without it the fruit may not be eaten

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is the view of Rabbi Akiva, taught without his name,
phrases.notes: "This" means the משנה's case of eating ביכורים before the reading.

phrases.english: but the Sages say:
For first fruits, placing is essential,
phrases.notes: Placing means setting the basket down beside the מזבח.

phrases.english: but reading is not essential.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְתִימְתָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה's ביכורים case from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's lashes for eating ביכורים before the קריאה follows רבי עקיבא. The חכמים hold that only הנחה is essential.

steps.title: Why not say it follows רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not say the משנה is רבי שמעון's unattributed view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say this is the view of רבי שמעון, taught without his name!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's choice of name. רבי שמעון seems to be a better fit for the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says this ruling openly, as we will soon see. So it seems more natural to credit the משנה to him than to רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him say; a suggestion that challenges what was said

phrases.english: But let him say this is the view
of Rabbi Shimon, taught without his name!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְתִימְתָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution made in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's naming of רבי עקיבא as the author of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון states this ruling openly, so he seems the more obvious author.

steps.title: The point is that רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן named רבי עקיבא on purpose, to teach that רבי עקיבא holds like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that רבי עקיבא holds like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Naming רבי עקיבא adds new information.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know רבי שמעון's view from his own words. By crediting רבי עקיבא, רבי יוחנן teaches something new: רבי עקיבא also holds this, even though he never said it openly.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
He holds; this is his opinion

phrases.english: This teaches us

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: that Rabbi Akiva holds like Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the wording teaches new information
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming רבי שמעון would be more natural, since he says the ruling openly.
steps.terutzMaskana: Naming רבי עקיבא teaches that he agrees with רבי שמעון.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון's view is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the view of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The גמרא is about to show us the source for רבי שמעון's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 14 and 15 assumed that רבי שמעון says this ruling openly. Now the גמרא will show where he says it.

keyTerms.meaning: What

phrases.english: What is the view of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view mentioned in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where רבי שמעון rules that eating ביכורים before the קריאה brings lashes.

steps.title: The פסוק's word 'gift of your hand' means ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that 'תרומת ידך' in the list of foods not to be eaten outside ירושלים refers to ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'and the gift of your hand' means ביכורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by bringing a ברייתא. This line sets up רבי שמעון's argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists foods that may not be eaten 'within your gates,' meaning outside ירושלים. The ברייתא first identifies 'תרומת ידך' as ביכורים, so that רבי שמעון can ask what this word is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The gift of your hand; read here as ביכורים

phrases.english: As it is taught: "and the gift of your hand"
these are first fruits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a ברייתא on the פסוק 'ותרומת ידך,' which refers to ביכורים.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: a קל וחומר already bans eating them outside the wall
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון asks what the word teaches. It cannot be the ban on eating ביכורים outside the wall, because a קל וחומר from מעשר שני already teaches that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: what does this come to teach us? If it means not to eat them outside the wall, that comes from a קל וחומר from מעשר, which is less strict. If someone who eats מעשר outside the wall gets lashes, then all the more so for ביכורים!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון shows that the word cannot mean the simple thing, since we would know it anyway. This sets up his real reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני is less holy than ביכורים, and eating it outside ירושלים brings lashes. So a קל וחומר teaches the same for ביכורים. A פסוק is not needed for something a קל וחומר already teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic from a lighter case to a stricter case
Here, מעשר שני, which is eaten in ירושלים
Outside the wall of ירושלים
Gets lashes
All the more so

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מָה בָּא זֶה לְלַמְּדֵנוּ?
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: What does this come to teach us?
If it teaches not to eat them outside the wall,
that comes from a kal vachomer from tithe, which is less strict:
If, for tithe, which is less strict,
one who eats it outside the wall gets lashes,
then for first fruits, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מָה בָּא זֶה לְלַמְּדֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the word identified in step 17 is teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'ותרומת ידך' as banning ביכורים outside the wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from מעשר already teaches that, so the פסוק would add nothing.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches lashes for eating before the קריאה
steps.stepSummary: So the פסוק must be teaching that a כהן who eats ביכורים before the reading gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק comes only to teach about one who eats ביכורים before the reading was said over them: he gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון concludes what the פסוק really teaches. This is the source the גמרא was looking for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the simple reading is already known from the קל וחומר, the word is used for a new rule. Eating ביכורים before the קריאה brings lashes. This shows that for רבי שמעון the reading is essential, which matches the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק
Said the ביכורים reading over them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון learns from 'ותרומת ידך' that eating ביכורים before the קריאה brings lashes, because a קל וחומר from מעשר already covers eating them outside the wall. רבי יוחנן teaches that רבי עקיבא agrees, while the חכמים hold that only הנחה is essential.

phrases.english: So the verse comes only
for one who eats from first fruits
before the reading was said over them,
teaching that he gets lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לֹא בָּא הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא לָאוֹכֵל מִבִּכּוּרִים עַד שֶׁלֹּא קָרָא עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the קל וחומר in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי שמעון, the פסוק teaches lashes for eating ביכורים before the קריאה. This matches the משנה and, according to רבי יוחנן, רבי עקיבא's view.

steps.title: 'Your gift offerings' means תודה and שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the word 'ונדבתיך' in the פסוק refers to תודה and שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Nor your gift offerings': these are the thanks-offering and the peace-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next word in the פסוק and says which קרבנות it refers to. This sets up רבי שמעון's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are voluntary offerings, which is why the פסוק calls them 'gifts.' This works the same way as step 17, where 'תרומת ידך' was explained as ביכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Your gift offerings: voluntary offerings
Thanks-offering
Peace-offerings, which have lighter holiness (קדשים קלים)

phrases.english: "Nor your gift offerings": this is a thanks-offering and peace-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the next item in the פסוק.

steps.title: רבי שמעון asks why the word is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון argues that the ban on eating תודה ושלמים outside ירושלים is already known through a קל וחומר from מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: What does this come to teach us? If it is about eating them outside the wall, we already know that through a קל וחומר from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון challenges the obvious reading of the word. It cannot be teaching the ban on eating outside the wall, because we already know that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני is not even a קרבן, yet one gets lashes for eating it outside the wall. So קרבנות, which are holier, must certainly carry the same rule. The word therefore needs a different job.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if the lighter case has the rule, the stricter case surely does
Outside the wall of ירושלים
Second tithe, which must be eaten in ירושלים

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
What does this come to teach us?
If it is about eating them outside the wall,
that comes from a kal vachomer from tithe,
phrases.notes: This means מעשר שני. It is not a קרבן, yet you get lashes for eating it outside the wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מָה בָּא זֶה לְלַמְּדֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain meaning of the word defined in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'ונדבתיך' teaches the ban on eating תודה ושלמים outside the wall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That ban is already known through a קל וחומר from מעשר שני, so the word would be extra.

steps.title: Eating תודה and שלמים before the blood is sprinkled brings lashes
steps.stepSummary: The word teaches that a person who eats תודה or שלמים before זריקה gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק comes only to teach about someone who eats from a תודה or שלמים before the sprinkling of the blood, that he gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives the word a new job. It teaches lashes for eating too early, before the blood was sprinkled on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat of a קרבן becomes permitted only after זריקה. The ban on eating outside the wall could be learned by logic, but this timing rule could not, so the פסוק is needed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the קרבן's blood on the מזבח, which permits the meat
He gets lashes

phrases.english: So the verse comes only
for one who eats of a thanks-offering or peace-offerings
before the sprinkling, that he gets lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 21 by giving the word a new teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Eating תודה or שלמים before זריקה carries lashes.

steps.title: 'Firstborn' means the בכור animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'ובכורות' refers to the firstborn animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or the firstborn': this is the בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next word in the פסוק. This sets up the next round of רבי שמעון's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is a firstborn kosher animal that is given to a כהן and brought as a קרבן. Only כהנים may eat its meat.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, given to a כהן and eaten only by כהנים

phrases.english: "Or the firstborn": this is the firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same ברייתא.

steps.title: Two קל וחומר arguments already cover the בכור
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says both the 'outside the wall' rule and the 'before זריקה' rule for a בכור are already known.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: What does this teach us? If it is about eating outside the wall, that comes from a קל וחומר from מעשר. If it is about eating before זריקה, that comes from a קל וחומר from תודה ושלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון now rules out two possible meanings. One is learned from מעשר, and the other from what we just learned about תודה ושלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 taught that eating lighter קרבנות before זריקה carries lashes. A בכור is holier, so it must have that rule too. Each new answer becomes the base for the next קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Before the blood is sprinkled

steps.confusionAlert: Watch how the list grows. Each conclusion (here, step 22) becomes the source for the next קל וחומר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
What does this come to teach us?
If it is about eating them outside the wall,
that comes from a kal vachomer from tithe;
if it is about eating before the sprinkling,
that comes from a kal vachomer from thanks-offering and peace-offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מָה בָּא זֶה לְלַמְּדֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 22 as a new source for a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'ובכורות' as teaching either the 'outside the wall' rule or the 'before זריקה' rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both rules already follow by קל וחומר, from מעשר and from תודה ושלמים.

steps.title: A non-כהן eating a בכור even after זריקה gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: The word teaches lashes for eating a בכור even after the blood is sprinkled, meaning a non-כהן who eats it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק comes only to teach about someone who eats from a בכור, even after זריקה, that he gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives 'בכורות' its own new teaching. Eating a בכור can carry lashes even at the time it is normally allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After זריקה, a בכור is permitted only to כהנים. So this rule is about a non-כהן who eats it. Nothing about תודה ושלמים could teach this, since anyone may eat those.

keyTerms.meaning: After the blood is sprinkled
A non-כהן

phrases.english: So the verse comes only
for one who eats from the firstborn
even after the sprinkling, that he gets lashes.
phrases.notes: He means a non-כהן. After the blood is sprinkled, a כהן is allowed to eat the בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A non-כהן who eats a בכור, even after זריקה, gets lashes.

steps.title: 'Your herd and flock' means חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'בקרך וצאנך' refers to the חטאת and the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Of your herd or of your flock': these are the sin-offering and the guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next word in the פסוק. This sets up the next round of רבי שמעון's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאת and אשם are קדשי קדשים, the holiest kind of קרבנות. Only כהנים may eat them, and only inside the courtyard of the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offering
Guilt-offering
The holiest קרבנות, eaten only inside the courtyard

phrases.english: "Of your herd or of your flock": this is a sin-offering and a guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בקרך וצאנך' refers to חטאת and אשם.

steps.title: Three קל וחומר arguments already cover חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules out three meanings: outside the wall, before זריקה, and a non-כהן eating after זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: What does this come to teach us? If it is about eating outside the wall, that comes from a קל וחומר from מעשר. If it is about eating before זריקה, that comes from תודה ושלמים. If it is about eating after זריקה, that comes from a קל וחומר from בכור!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון finishes his question by ruling out every rule taught so far. Each one already applies to the holier חטאת and אשם by קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 25 (a non-כהן eating a בכור after זריקה) now becomes the third source. Since חטאת and אשם are holier than a בכור, all three rules apply to them automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from the lighter case of the בכור

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מָה בָּא זֶה לְלַמְּדֵנוּ?
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: What does this come to teach us?
If it is about eating them outside the wall,
that comes from a kal vachomer from tithe;
if it is about eating before the sprinkling,
that comes from a kal vachomer from thanks-offering and peace-offerings;
if it is about eating after the sprinkling,
that comes from a kal vachomer from the firstborn!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מָה בָּא זֶה לְלַמְּדֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the conclusion of step 25 as a third קל וחומר source.
steps.kashyaTarget: Any reading of 'בקרך וצאנך' that repeats rules already known.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All three earlier rules carry over to the holier חטאת and אשם by קל וחומר.

steps.title: Eating חטאת and אשם outside the courtyard brings lashes
steps.stepSummary: The word teaches lashes for eating חטאת or אשם outside the courtyard, even after זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק comes only to teach about someone who eats from a חטאת or אשם, even after זריקה, outside the curtains, that he gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives the last word its new teaching. Even a כהן eating at the right time gets lashes if he eats these קרבנות outside the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail here is place. חטאת and אשם must be eaten inside the courtyard, which the curtains surrounded in the משכן. No lighter case teaches this, since those can be eaten anywhere in ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the curtains, meaning outside the courtyard of the משכן or מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's pattern: whenever a word's plain rule can be learned by קל וחומר, the word must teach a new prohibition that carries lashes. So far the results are ביכורים before the reading, תודה ושלמים before זריקה, a non-כהן eating a בכור after זריקה, and eating חטאת ואשם outside the courtyard. The next steps add one more word, נדריך, for the עולה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי שמעון gives lashes in many cases that the plain פסוק does not seem to list. The ביכורים part of this list (step 19) is the ruling that רבי יוחנן says רבי עקיבא shares (step 15).

phrases.english: So the verse comes only
for one who eats from a sin-offering or guilt-offering
even after the sprinkling
outside the curtains, that he gets lashes.
phrases.notes: The curtains surrounded the courtyard of the משכן. The ban covers eating anywhere outside the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Eating חטאת or אשם outside the courtyard, even after זריקה, carries lashes.

steps.title: The word 'your vows' means the burnt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the word נדריך in the פסוק refers to the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Your vows": this is the burnt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next word in the פסוק and says נדריך is talking about the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each earlier word in the פסוק was linked to a different holy food: ביכורים, then תודה and שלמים, then בכור, then חטאת and אשם. Now נדריך is linked to the עולה, which is the holiest of all, because it is burned completely on the מזבח and nobody eats it. This sets up רבי שמעון's question about what new lesson the word can teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Your vows, a word in the פסוק about eating holy food (דברים 12:17)
Burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח
The holiest group of קרבנות, which includes the עולה

phrases.english: "Your vows": this is the burnt-offering.
phrases.notes: דברים 12:17. A person usually brings an עולה because of a promise he made, so it fits the word 'vows'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next word in the same ברייתא, after בקרך וצאנך was linked to חטאת and אשם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word נדריך in the פסוק refers to the עולה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון shows every possible lesson is already known
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון asks what נדריך teaches, since four possible lashes-rules for an עולה can each be learned by a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: What does this come to teach us? If it is for eating it outside the wall, that comes from a קל וחומר from מעשר. If it is for eating before זריקה, that comes from a קל וחומר from תודה and שלמים. If it is for eating after זריקה, that comes from a קל וחומר from בכור. If it is for eating outside the curtains, that comes from a קל וחומר from חטאת and אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון challenges the word: every lesson we might think it teaches about an עולה is already known by logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case uses a less holy קרבן that already has the rule. Since the עולה is holier, it should have the rule even more. מעשר may not be eaten outside the wall, תודה and שלמים not before זריקה, a בכור not by a non-כהן even after זריקה, and חטאת and אשם not outside the courtyard. So the word must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does this come to teach us? Used when a word seems unnecessary
Logic from a lighter case to a stricter one: if the lighter case has the rule, the stricter one surely does
Second tithe, eaten only inside ירושלים
Thanks-offering and peace-offering, which have lighter holiness
Firstborn animal, eaten only by כהנים
Outside the curtains, meaning outside the courtyard of the משכן or בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the word נדריך is useless. רבי שמעון is only showing it cannot mean any of these four rules, so it must teach a fifth one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
What does this come to teach us?
If it is for eating them outside the wall,
that is a קל וחומר from tithe;
if it is for eating before the sprinkling,
that is a קל וחומר from thanks-offering and peace-offering;
if it is for eating after the sprinkling,
that is a קל וחומר from the firstborn;
if it is for eating outside the curtains,
that is a קל וחומר from sin-offering and guilt-offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מָה בָּא זֶה לְלַמְּדֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the word נדריך that step 29 linked to the עולה
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word נדריך as a source for lashes about an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every possible rule for an עולה already follows by קל וחומר from a less holy קרבן that has that rule, so the word seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Setting up the real lesson of the word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to say what the word נדריך really comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse comes...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the answer. The גמרא starts saying what the word truly teaches, and the sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four simple rules were ruled out, so the word must teach a new rule that a קל וחומר cannot give. This follows the same pattern as steps 25 and 28.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; so then
Comes only to teach; a phrase that opens the real lesson
The verse

phrases.english: Rather, the verse comes
phrases.notes: Literally 'the verse did not come,' but here it means 'it comes only to teach.' The sentence goes on in the next line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to רבי שמעון's challenge in step 30
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The word נדריך teaches a new lashes-rule for an עולה that the four קל וחומר cases cannot cover. The rule itself is stated in the continuation.
